slides.title: Understand storage pressure
keyPoints: df -hT reports filesystem block capacity and type. df -i reports inode capacity. du -x -h DIRECTORY accounts for reachable directory entries on one filesystem. findmnt --target PATH identifies the containing mount. lsof +L1 can identify ope
slides.narration: df -hT reports filesystem block capacity and type. df -i reports inode capacity. du -x -h DIRECTORY accounts for reachable directory entries on one filesystem. findmnt --target PATH identifies the containing mount. lsof +L1 can identify open unlinked files, subject to access and scope. None of these commands alone identifies every cause of a full filesystem. See Chapters 9, 21, 23, and 32.

slides.title: Understand a systemd service
keyPoints: systemctl status NAME.service --no-pager provides a useful summary. systemctl cat NAME.service shows unit files and drop-ins. systemctl show NAME.service exposes manager properties. journalctl -u NAME.service --since '-10 minutes' retrieves
slides.narration: systemctl status NAME.service --no-pager provides a useful summary. systemctl cat NAME.service shows unit files and drop-ins. systemctl show NAME.service exposes manager properties. journalctl -u NAME.service --since '-10 minutes' retrieves a time-scoped log view. slides.title: Validate a candidate before applying it
keyPoints: bash -n SCRIPT checks Bash syntax, not behavior. sshd -t validates SSH server configuration, not every user’s ability to log in. nginx -t validates the complete NGINX configuration and some referenced resources, not the entire client path.
slides.narration: bash -n SCRIPT checks Bash syntax, not behavior. sshd -t validates SSH server configuration, not every user’s ability to log in. nginx -t validates the complete NGINX configuration and some referenced resources, not the entire client path. findmnt --verify --tab-file FILE inspects an fstab candidate, not every future storage condition. A validation command is one gate, followed by application-level verification and recovery planning.

slides.title: Read an error as evidence
keyPoints: Record the exact command, host, identity, timestamp, exit status, and relevant output. Separate a refused connection from a timeout, an absent DNS name from a resolver that cannot answer, a permission denial from a nonexistent path, and a f
slides.narration: Record the exact command, host, identity, timestamp, exit status, and relevant output. Separate a refused connection from a timeout, an absent DNS name from a resolver that cannot answer, a permission denial from a nonexistent path, and a full filesystem from a full directory assumption. These distinctions reduce both wasted effort and dangerous changes.
